video.title: How a machine works, in under a minute
video.description: Sample 01: an English narrated, AI-assisted concept film following one workpiece through a fictional machine, from input to output. The machine is illustrative, not a real product or engineering reference.
video.label: Fictional concept sample · English narration
transcript: A machine is easier to understand when you can follow the work. Start with one part entering the line.
Inside, a sequence of stages turns a complicated system into a process you can see.
The important story is how the work moves from one stage to the next: what comes in, what happens in between, and what comes out.
When customers can follow that sequence, they have a clearer way to understand where the machine fits and what to ask next.

faqs.question: What belongs in a product video library?
faqs.answer: Start with recurring customer questions: product overviews, workflow explainers, setup orientations and service topics. Use product-approved references and keep each story focused.

faqs.question: Can a short video replace a manual or safety instructions?
faqs.answer: No. Videos can help explain a product or workflow, but approved manuals, safety information and formal instructions remain authoritative.

faqs.question: How should categories be organized?
faqs.answer: Use categories customers recognize, such as product family, application or customer task. Test the structure with sales, onboarding and service teams.

faqs.question: Can the same video be used in sales and support?
faqs.answer: Some general explainers may work across moments. Setup, safety and maintenance content should be specific to its audience, product and approved instructions.
